notes.claim: RC is the time in which a discharging capacitor's charge drops to 1/e of its starting value, and it has dimensions of time, so it is called the time constant.
In the first time constant after the switch is closed, a discharging capacitor's voltage falls to 0.368 of its initial value.
Newton's law of cooling says an object cools or warms at a rate proportional to the gap between its temperature and the surroundings' temperature.
Newton's law of cooling holds only for very small temperature differences, so a hot part follows the capacitor-like curve only approximately.
In exponential decay the rate of change is proportional to the current value.
In insulation testing the capacitive charging current quickly falls to zero, the same shrinking charging current as a capacitor charging through a resistor (Megger, notes 7.3).
A trade tutorial (SECONDARY) treats a capacitor as fully charged after five time constants, at 99.3%: a convention, since it never reaches 100% (notes 4.4).
IEC 60831, as a trade page reports it (SECONDARY), requires power factor correction capacitors to discharge to below 75 V within 3 minutes (notes 7.2).

sources.quote: Newton’s law of cooling states that an object will cool (or warm) at a rate that is proportional to the difference between the temperature of the object and the ambient temperature T a of its surroundings.
